subject: Quantify AI — Dedicated pool sizing & flex-commit pricing
messages:
From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@quantify.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Chen <maya.chen@quantify.ai>, procurement@quantify.ai
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool inquiry and pricing questions

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the call earlier — Quantify is moving to production on a retrieval-augmented generation feature and we need a predictable pricing and capacity plan. A few key asks from procurement and engineering:

- We need a baseline committed pool that covers 95% of steady-state traffic, with a clear path for ~2x bursting for marketing campaigns.
- Can you provide a recommended GPU pool size (model type / count) based on the workload below?
- Pricing: we want a 12–24 month reserved pricing proposal and visibility into discounts for longer commits.

Workload (initial estimate):
- Average request volume: 320k requests/day (weekdays), 50k/day (weekends)
- Typical peak 5-min QPS during business hours: 450 qps; sustained peak (1h): 200 qps
- Average prompt+response token length: 180 tokens/respond (prompt ~60, response ~120)
- Retrieval stage adds 4–8KB per request of context; end-to-end latency target: p95 < 350ms
- Model: expect to serve a mix (mainly Llama-3-70B-quantized for generation plus a smaller encoder for reranking)
- Concurrency pattern: highly chatty, many short sessions; cold start tolerance is low

Attached is a CSV sample of hourly traffic for the last 30 days. Procurement wants a written proposal to compare against another vendor.

Can you respond with a sizing model and pricing bands?

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Product, Quantify AI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@quantify.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool inquiry and pricing questions

Alex — thanks for the detail and the sample. I sketched a quick sizing pass and a flexible commit proposal so you can compare TCO and burst behavior. High level summary up front:

- Recommended committed baseline: 6 x H100-equivalent GPUs (Redwood’s "rH100-small") to meet p95 <350ms for your stated mix, with automatic KV/prefix caching for common prompts.
- Burst capacity: 2x burst credits (elastic pool) that can be consumed for short campaigns. We model this as 12x equivalent GPUs available for up to 4 hours/day or credits applied for longer bursts.
- Pricing band: baseline reserved commit (12 mo) = $X/month (see spreadsheet). 24-mo commit ~12% discount on monthly rate; 36-mo ~20% and includes 20% additional burst credits.

I need a couple of confirmations to finalize the SOW: exact model variants (do you require L3-70B fp16 or can you accept q4f16 quantized weights for generation?), expected RW (read/write) latency from retrieval store, and whether the reranker must be colocated on the same GPU pool.

I’m attaching a short deck and an example pricing workbook. Will incorporate Ben’s proposed SLA language and Lauren can include billing/commit mechanics.

—Jordan
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Maya Chen <maya.chen@quantify.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@quantify.ai>, procurement@quantify.ai
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool inquiry and pricing questions

Jordan — quick follow with clarifications from infra and procurement:

- Model: We can accept quantized weights for the generation model (q4f16 acceptable) but want a fallback to fp16 for long-context threads (>=8k tokens) where quality drops.
- Retrieval store: Redis/TiKV in same VPC with median RTT 6ms; we expect the retrieval stage to add ~20ms typical.
- Reranker: needs to be colocated to avoid additional network hops.
- Contract target: prefer 24-month but procurement wants a midpoint option (18-month) and explicit exit terms for capacity over/underutilization.

Let us know if the 6x H100 baseline still stands with that fallback requirement.

Thanks,
Maya
Engineering Lead, Quantify AI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Chen <maya.chen@quantify.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool inquiry and pricing questions

Maya — thanks, that helps. Updated recommendation and rationale below (TL;DR first):

- Baseline: 6 x rH100-small GPUs (each rH100-small ~= 80 TFLOPS fp16 effective for generation, optimized kernels and continuous batching). This baseline supports ~500 qps mixed-gen at moderate response lengths with p95 < 350ms when using quantized weights.
- Fallback for long context: add 1 x rH100-large (hot-standby special) that holds fp16 weights for sessions that exceed 8k tokens; routing policy will steer those sessions to the fp16 instance and keep others on quantized nodes. Expect a small increase in p95 for those routed requests (~+60ms) but improved quality.
- Reranker colocated: allocate 1 x rA40-medium (cost-efficient inference GPU) for the encoder/reranker colocated in the same pool — minimal cost and reduces end-to-end latency by ~10–15ms vs crossing nodes.
- Burst: elastic credits to reach 12x capacity for up to 4 hours/day. Credits are priced and can be used up to 10 days/month; unused credits roll over up to 30 days.

Sizing rationale: we simulated your sample traffic with average tokens=180, median response tokens 120, and saw that continuous batching with dynamic batching windows of 8–15ms gives best throughput/latency tradeoff. The 6x baseline assumes a 70/30 split of generation to reranking traffic and a 10% headroom for small traffic growth.

Pricing mechanics (summary):
- 12-mo reserve: list rate = $Y/month per rH100-small; committed discount tiers: 10% (@12mo), 18% (@18mo), 24% (@24mo) off list.
- Add-on: fp16 hot-standby billed at 50% of a full rH100-small because it won't be used for steady state; reranker rA40-medium billed as fixed monthly line item.
- SLA: 99.9% availability for the dedicated pool, with credits for target misses.

Ben — can you confirm that the discount ladder and burst-credit pricing look good from a pricing+finance perspective? Lauren, happy to have you draft the exit clauses Maya mentioned.

Jordan
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Chen <maya.chen@quantify.ai>, Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@quantify.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantify AI — Dedicated pool sizing & flex-commit pricing

Jordan / team — quick pricing confirmation from my side:

- Discount ladder is fine; we can firm 18% at 18 months as a midpoint option (procurement asked for) if they commit to minimum 85% utilization of committed baseline over contract term.
- Burst credits: priced at 0.6x equivalent of committed monthly unit rate per credit-hour. We provide 120 credit-hours/month as standard with the 24-mo plan, 90 credit-hours for 18-mo, 60 for 12-mo. Additional credits can be purchased at standard add-on rates.
- Exit clause: for underutilization we propose a true-up at 6-month intervals (standard in enterprise deals). If average utilization <60% for two consecutive quarters, Quantify can reduce baseline to 4x rH100-small with a 60-day notice and a 3-month pro-rated reconciliation.

I’ll add these as terms in the SOW draft. Approving for commercial review.

—Ben
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@quantify.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quantify AI — Dedicated pool sizing & flex-commit pricing

Jordan / Ben — this looks good and aligns with what procurement was hoping for. A couple of quick asks before we sign:

1) Can you add a performance runbook (2 pages) describing steps for capacity-related incidents (how routing to burst works, fallback policies, rollback to previous model versions)?
2) Please include a sample invoice schedule showing monthly vs quarterly billing for the 18-month option.

If you can drop those two items, we’ll route to legal next week and aim for a mid-October start.

Thanks — Alex
--- End of thread ---
